# Designit

> Designit is a senior-led, research-led product design studio in Noida, India. It helps SaaS, technology and enterprise teams understand their users, simplify complex products, redesign experiences and build scalable design systems, working with clients in India, the United States, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

This file is a plain-text summary of designit.co.in for AI assistants. It mirrors what the website says; it adds nothing that is not on the site. A complete page index is at [llms-full.txt](https://designit.co.in/llms-full.txt).

## What is Designit?

Designit is a senior-led, research-led product design studio in Noida, India. It helps SaaS, technology and enterprise teams understand their users, simplify complex products, redesign experiences and build scalable design systems, working with clients in India, the United States, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

**Disambiguation:** Designit Studio (designit.co.in) is an independent product design studio headquartered in Noida, India. It is not affiliated with Designit A/S, the Aarhus-founded design consultancy owned by Wipro.

**Founder:** Sahil Sharma, a product designer with more than ten years of experience ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/best-design-studio/)). [About the studio](https://designit.co.in/about/).

## Why teams choose Designit

- **Senior people only** — No account managers and no junior hand-off after the pitch. You work with the people doing the design.
- **Research-led** — Every engagement starts with evidence: research, analytics or an audit, before design decisions.
- **Founder-led** — Founded by Sahil Sharma, a product designer with more than ten years of experience.
- **Named, published work** — 22 case studies across Adda247, Kelp Global, Betacrew, the Omniyat portfolio and Tata Elxsi.
- **Four markets** — Clients in India, the United States, the United Kingdom and the UAE.

## How we work

One method across every engagement, run by senior designers from kickoff to handover.

1. **Research: Find out what is actually happening** — Interviews, usability testing and your analytics, before anyone argues about solutions.
2. **Strategy: Agree the problem in writing** — A signed-off definition of what we are solving and how success is measured.
3. **Experience design: Structure first, then interface** — Information architecture and flows, then UI designed against real data and constraints.
4. **Validation: Test while changes are cheap** — Prototypes tested with people who match your users.
5. **Systems: Make it consistent and buildable** — Design systems and developer-ready handoff, with design QA against what ships.
6. **Evolution: Keep improving after launch** — Measurement against the agreed metric, and ongoing design capacity if you need it.

Designit designs, specifies and supports build through design QA and launch support. Development itself is done by the client's team or development partner.

## Services

All services: [https://designit.co.in/services/](https://designit.co.in/services/)

### UX Research

Page: [UX Research](https://designit.co.in/services/ux-research/)

**Research that turns product uncertainty into decisions**

*When should product teams invest in research?*

Invest in research when a decision is expensive to reverse, when the team is not the user, or when a credible internal disagreement has stalled progress. Otherwise, intuition plus a fast experiment is often better value.

Research methods: User interviews; Usability testing; Contextual research; Competitive research; Journey mapping; Concept testing; Information architecture research; Heuristic evaluation; Quantitative analysis, where available.

### UX Audit

Page: [UX Audit](https://designit.co.in/services/ux-audit/)

**Find the friction before it costs you users**

*What is a UX audit?*

A UX audit is a structured evaluation of a digital product or website that identifies usability problems, interaction friction, accessibility issues and conversion blockers, and ranks the fixes by impact and effort.

What problems can a UX audit reveal? Onboarding drop-off; Features nobody can find; Leaks on high-intent pages; Forms and error states; Inconsistency that reads as risk; Accessibility gaps.

### Product Design

Page: [Product Design](https://designit.co.in/services/product-design/)

**Product design that turns complexity into usable experiences**

*What product design solves*

Product design decides what a digital product should do, how it is structured and how it behaves, so that people can get real work done with it and the business can keep growing it.

What we cover: Discovery; Research; Information architecture; User flows; UX design; UI design; Prototyping; Validation; Design systems; Developer handoff.

### SaaS Product Design

Page: [SaaS Product Design](https://designit.co.in/services/saas-product-design/)

**SaaS product design for complex B2B products**

*What makes SaaS UX difficult?*

SaaS UX is difficult because the buyer is rarely the user, the work is dense by necessity, and the edge cases (permissions, bulk actions, partial data, very large accounts) are everyday reality rather than exceptions.

When does a SaaS product need redesign? Users sign up and never activate; The dashboard shows everything and says nothing; Every screen looks like a different product; Enterprise deals stall at the demo; New features have nowhere to go.

### Mobile App Design

Page: [Mobile App Design](https://designit.co.in/services/mobile-app-design/)

**Mobile app design for products people open every day**

A mobile app gets seconds of attention, on a small screen, often on an unreliable connection. We design apps around the one or two jobs people open them for, and make those jobs fast, forgiving and native to each platform.

Why mobile apps lose users: Onboarding asks before it gives; Permission prompts at the wrong moment; Navigation built for a desktop product; Forms that fight the keyboard; Fragile on real networks.

### AI Product Design

Page: [AI Product Design](https://designit.co.in/services/ai-product-design/)

**Designing AI products people can understand and trust**

*What changes when a product becomes AI-powered?*

When a product becomes AI-powered, its output stops being fully predictable: the same input can produce different results, results can be confidently wrong, and the system may act on the user's behalf. Design has to make that uncertainty visible, checkable and correctable.

AI interaction patterns: Suggest and accept; Draft, then edit; Ask to clarify; Streaming with control; Sources and grounding; Scoped automation.

### UI/UX Design

Page: [UI/UX Design](https://designit.co.in/services/ui-ux-design/)

**A UI/UX design studio for software people use every day**

*What does a UI/UX design company do?*

A UI/UX design company researches how people use a product, structures it so they can find their way, and designs the interface and interactions they work with, then supports engineers so the shipped product matches the design.

What usually brings teams to us: The interface grew rather than got designed; Design is a bottleneck, not a multiplier; It looks fine and performs badly; You've outgrown a freelancer.

### Design System Development

Page: [Design System Development](https://designit.co.in/services/design-systems/)

**Design systems that help product teams ship consistently**

*When do you need a design system?*

You need a design system when several people ship in parallel across several surfaces and inconsistency has started to slow delivery or show up in sales conversations. Below roughly one product and two designers, a shared style file is usually enough.

Signs your product has outgrown ad-hoc UI: It exists, and nobody uses it; Design and code have drifted; It covers the happy path only; Every new surface starts from scratch.

### Conversion Optimization

Page: [Conversion Optimization](https://designit.co.in/services/conversion-optimization/)

**Conversion optimization through better product experience**

*What causes conversion friction?*

Conversion friction comes from moments where a motivated visitor cannot understand the offer, does not trust it enough, or finds the next step too hard: unclear value, missing proof, surprise costs, long forms and errors with no way to recover.

Where conversion is won or lost: Landing-page conversion; SaaS conversion; Checkout friction; Activation; Onboarding; Lead qualification.

### Website Design

Page: [Website Design](https://designit.co.in/services/website-design/)

**Websites built to explain, convince and convert**

*Website strategy*

Website strategy decides who the site is for, what each of those visitors needs to believe before they act, and what action is right for each stage of intent. Design and copy follow from those answers.

Why websites underperform: They describe, they don't explain; The structure mirrors the org chart; Every page asks for a meeting; Proof is buried; Templates stretched past their limit.

### Branding

Page: [Branding](https://designit.co.in/services/branding/)

**Brand systems for technology companies ready to grow**

*Brand strategy*

Brand strategy defines who the company is for, what it stands for, and why a buyer should believe it, before any logo is drawn. It is the brief that every visual and verbal decision is checked against.

Brand research: Customer and buyer interviews; Competitive audit; Perception review.

## Solutions

Engagements organised around a business situation rather than a deliverable. Hub: [https://designit.co.in/solutions/](https://designit.co.in/solutions/)

### MVP Design

Page: [MVP Design](https://designit.co.in/solutions/mvp-design/)

**MVP design: launch the smallest product that proves the point**

*What should you do first?*

Before designing an MVP, write down the one assumption the first release must prove, such as that a specific user will complete a specific job with your product, and design only what is needed to test it convincingly.

### Product Redesign

Page: [Product Redesign](https://designit.co.in/solutions/product-redesign/)

**Product redesign without breaking what already works**

*What should you do first?*

Before a redesign, establish with evidence which journeys lose users and why. Then fix the structure (navigation, information architecture, flows) before the visual layer, because restyling a broken structure preserves the problem.

### Legacy Product Modernization

Page: [Legacy Product Modernization](https://designit.co.in/solutions/legacy-product-modernization/)

**Modernise a legacy product without stopping the business**

*What should you do first?*

Map how people actually use the legacy product, including the workarounds and the spreadsheets beside it, before changing anything. Workarounds are requirements the original design never captured.

### Design System Scaling

Page: [Design System Scaling](https://designit.co.in/solutions/design-system-scaling/)

**Scale a design system across products and teams**

*What should you do first?*

Separate what is shared from what is product-specific. A system scales when its foundations (tokens, type, spacing, accessibility rules) are shared, its components are configurable, and product-specific patterns live in their own layer.

### Conversion Improvement

Page: [Conversion Improvement](https://designit.co.in/solutions/conversion-improvement/)

**Improve conversion by fixing the experience, not the button colour**

*What should you do first?*

Find out whether low conversion is a traffic problem (the wrong people arrive), an offer problem (the right people don't want it at that price) or an experience problem (the right people want it and can't get through). Only the third is fixed by design.

## Industries

Hub: [https://designit.co.in/industries/](https://designit.co.in/industries/)

### B2B SaaS

Page: [B2B SaaS](https://designit.co.in/industries/b2b-saas/)

**B2B SaaS product design for complex workflows**

*Why SaaS products become difficult to use*

SaaS products become difficult to use because they grow by accretion: each feature is added where there is room, navigation built for version one has to absorb version ten, and edge cases such as permissions, bulk actions and very large accounts are handled one at a time instead of designed as a system.

SaaS UX challenges we work on: Onboarding; Dashboards; Navigation; Feature adoption; Permissions; Design systems.

### AI Products

Page: [AI Products](https://designit.co.in/industries/ai/)

**Product design for AI startups and AI-native software**

AI products fail less often on model quality than on product design: people don't know what to ask, can't tell when to trust the answer, and can't follow what an agent did. We design the product around the model so it gets used, and used safely.

Who we work with: AI startups; AI SaaS; Agentic products.

### Fintech

Page: [Fintech](https://designit.co.in/industries/fintech/)

**Fintech design, where trust is a feature and regulation is a constraint**

*What makes fintech design harder than it looks*

Fintech design is hard because trust is decided in seconds, regulation fixes much of what you must ask, and mistakes such as a wrong transfer can't be undone. The design job is to make required steps feel safe, understandable and recoverable.

What we design for fintech: Trust; KYC; Onboarding; Data density; Financial workflows; Compliance-sensitive UX; Dashboards; Transactional confidence.

### EdTech

Page: [EdTech](https://designit.co.in/industries/edtech/)

**EdTech design measured by completion, not by enrolment**

Signing learners up is a marketing problem. Getting them to finish is a design problem, and it decides whether an education product actually works. We have designed modules across one of India's largest exam-preparation platforms.

What EdTech design has to solve: Motivation is the real constraint; High stakes, low tolerance; Two users, one product; The device is not a flagship phone.

### PropTech & Real Estate

Page: [PropTech & Real Estate](https://designit.co.in/industries/real-estate/)

**PropTech and real estate design, where the website is the first viewing**

For a high-value development, the digital experience is where a buyer decides whether to take the call. We design property platforms that hold attention long enough to produce a qualified enquiry, not a form fill from someone who will never transact.

What property design actually has to solve: Enquiry volume is the wrong metric; Luxury is communicated through restraint; The assets are enormous; Gulf markets are not a translation job.

### E-commerce

Page: [E-commerce](https://designit.co.in/industries/e-commerce/)

**E-commerce design judged on revenue per visitor, not aesthetics**

Most online stores lose buyers at a few specific points, usually the product page, the cart and the first checkout step. We find which one is costing you most, then design the fix and measure it.

Where online retail actually loses money: The product page doesn't answer the objection; Checkout asks too much, too early; Mobile is the majority and the afterthought; Acquisition subsidises a leaky funnel.

### Automotive HMI

Page: [Automotive HMI](https://designit.co.in/industries/automotive/)

**In-car design where a second of attention is the budget**

Automotive HMI is one place where an interface decision has a physical safety consequence. We design infotainment and cluster experiences around glance duration and cognitive load, constraints that make most conventional UI thinking actively wrong.

Why automotive HMI breaks normal design rules: Attention is borrowed, not given; The user is physically moving; Hardware is fixed years ahead; Safety-critical and comfort share a screen.

## Clients and case studies

Published case studies: [https://designit.co.in/projects/](https://designit.co.in/projects/). Outcomes are described qualitatively; the site does not publish client metrics it cannot verify.

### Adda247 — EdTech

Case study: [Adda247](https://designit.co.in/projects/adda247/)

- Product: Competitive-exam preparation platform: web, Android, iOS and iPad
- Services: UX research, product design, design system, mobile app design
- Problem: A platform that grew module by module needed one coherent learning experience across tests, live classes, dashboards and community.
- What was delivered: Redesigned modules including the test-series engine, live classes, performance dashboards, community and native iOS/iPad apps.

### Kelp Global — B2B SaaS

Case study: [Kelp Global](https://designit.co.in/projects/kelp-global/)

- Product: CRM intelligence suite: Chrome extension, Truenorth analytics dashboard, deals module
- Services: SaaS product design, dashboard design, design system
- Problem: Sales teams were switching between tools to find contact intelligence, read pipeline health and manage deals.
- What was delivered: Three connected products designed on one shared design system.

### Betacrew — Developer tools

Case study: [Betacrew](https://designit.co.in/projects/betacrew/)

- Product: Portle, a developer-first API management platform
- Services: Product design, developer UX, white-label design system
- Problem: Developers managed APIs across three disconnected tools for design, testing and documentation, so documentation drifted out of date.
- What was delivered: One platform replacing three tools, with a white-label theming system for enterprise deployments.

### R-Centric (Omniyat portfolio) — PropTech and real estate

Case study: [R-Centric (Omniyat portfolio)](https://designit.co.in/projects/rcentric/)

- Product: Luxury property websites for seven Dubai developments
- Services: Website design, design system
- Problem: Each property launch needed a premium digital experience without starting from scratch every time.
- What was delivered: Seven property experiences delivered on a shared system that kept each launch distinct.

### Tata Elxsi — Automotive HMI

Case study: [Tata Elxsi](https://designit.co.in/projects/tata-elxsi/)

- Product: In-car infotainment system and digital instrument cluster
- Services: Product design, HMI design
- Problem: In-car interfaces where every glance is attention taken from the road, inside a tier-one supplier's hardware constraints.
- What was delivered: Two HMI systems designed: an infotainment interface and a digital instrument cluster.

## Frequently asked questions

Answers as published on the homepage.

**What types of companies do you work with?**

Mainly B2B SaaS companies, fintech and Web3 startups, AI products, EdTech platforms, e-commerce brands and enterprise software teams across India, the UAE, the US and the UK, typically funded startups and growth-stage companies redesigning a product, building a design system or making design a growth lever. Shipped work includes Adda247, StudyIQ, Kelp Global, Tata Elxsi, Betacrew and the Omniyat portfolio.

**How long does a typical project take?**

A focused landing page or marketing-site sprint runs two to three weeks, a complete product redesign or new SaaS dashboard six to ten weeks, and a full design system eight to twelve weeks. Single-feature design sprints can ship in five working days.

**What's your design process like?**

Research, strategy, experience design, validation, systems and evolution. In practice: a fast onboarding, about a week of research and discovery, two to three weeks of design and iteration, and a handoff with developer specs and implementation support, with async updates throughout and one short weekly sync.

**What tools do you use?**

Figma as the primary canvas; FigJam or Miro for workshops; Figma, Framer or Protopie for prototypes; Maze, Lookback or Lyssna for testing; and Notion, Slack, Loom and Linear for project work. We happily work inside your team's tools.

**What are your pricing models?**

Project-based fixed pricing for defined scopes, monthly retainers for ongoing partnerships (typically ₹1.5L to ₹4L a month depending on hours), and design subscriptions with a flat monthly fee. Pricing scales with complexity, team size and timeline, and you get a tailored quote after a discovery call.
